subject: POC: Acme - Evaluation plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acme.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC: Acme - Evaluation plan & success criteria

Hi Tom / Sarah —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through the product goals and the key pain points (latency spikes on peak, unpredictable per-token cost, and integration complexity). As discussed on the call, we propose a 4-week POC focused on two evaluation tracks: offline evals (representative prompt set + rubric) and an online shadow run against a subset of live requests. The objective is to validate:

- Success criteria:
  - Latency: p95 under 350ms for customer-route traffic during business hours
  - Cost: >= 30% reduction in per-token spend for the evaluated routes vs current baseline
  - Accuracy/quality: >= 90% pass rate on rubric graded offline prompts (see rubric tab)
  - Reliability: seamless fallback to secondary model under load without >1% error rate

- Proposed timeline:
  - Week 0 (this week): finalize eval scope, sample data, and rubric.
  - Week 1: offline evals on curated prompt set; baseline metrics collected.
  - Week 2: deploy shadow traffic for routed subset (non-prod) and compare online metrics.
  - Week 3: iterate on config (batching/quantization) and retest.
  - Week 4: final report and recommended rollout plan.

- Ownership:
  - Redwood: setup shadow routing, run offline evals, provide config recommendations (Dylan + Marissa).
  - Acme: provide sample prompt set and baseline logs, identify 1-2 engineer owners for shadow routing (Tom/Sarah).

Attached: acme-poc-eval-plan.pdf (plan + timeline) and acme-eval-rubric.xlsx (draft grading rubric). Please review and confirm:

1) The success criteria above reflect what we discussed?
2) Are the dates / 4-week cadence feasible on your side?
3) Who will be the internal owners for sample data and shadow rollout?

If this looks good I’ll send a short mutual action plan and propose kickoff on Wed 23 June.

Thanks —
Dylan

--

Subject: Re: POC: Acme - Evaluation plan & success criteria

Thanks Dylan — this looks like a good summary. A few notes from our side:

- Success criteria: we agree on latency and cost targets; for quality/rubric, can we add a category for hallucination rate (we measure hallucinations as incorrect factual assertions for prompts classified as "fact-based"). We’d like hallucination < 5% on that subset.
- Timeline: 4 weeks is fine but can you build in a 2-day buffer between Week 2 and Week 3 for our infra team to approve routing changes?
- Owners: I’ll be the exec sponsor. Sarah will be the day-to-day eng owner and will loop in our infrastructure engineer (Mark O.) for routing work.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you provide a sample offline prompt set template (CSV) we can use to export from our platform?
2) For the shadow run, will Redwood need VPN access or can we run via public endpoints with token-based auth?

Happy to kickoff Wed 23rd at 10am ET if that still works.

- Tom

Hi Tom / Dylan / Sarah —

Thanks — I’ve attached an updated rubric (acme-eval-rubric.xlsx) and a sample prompt CSV template in the plan PDF. A few methodology notes to align on offline vs online:

- Offline evals (Week 1):
  - We’ll run a stratified sample of ~600 prompts across the categories you mentioned on the call (support responses, product descriptions, fact-based lookups).
  - Each prompt will be graded by our evaluation script and then spot-checked by a human rater. Grading rubric columns: correctness (0/1), helpfulness (1-5), hallucination flag (0/1), confidence notes.
  - Thresholds: offline pass = >= 90% correctness and <= 5% hallucination on fact-based prompts.

- Online shadow (Week 2):
  - Shadow will receive a 10% replica of production routing for selected routes (non-customer-facing). Requests will be logged but responses returned to production system unchanged.
  - We will compute p95 latency, error rate, and compare top-line rubric proxies (automated heuristics for hallucination and token-efficiency).
  - Buffer: we’ll include the 2-day buffer Tom requested before Week 3 for infra sign-off.

- Ownership & deliverables:
  - Redwood: deliver weekly interim report (Wednesdays), final report with config recommendations and cost/latency comparisons.
  - Acme: provide prompt CSV & baseline logs by Tue 29 Jun; confirm infra contact for routing.

Next steps I’ll take after kickoff: finalize the prompt CSV template with your exported sample, run the offline batch, and share the first interim report.

Let me know if you want the rubric thresholds tightened; otherwise I’ll lock the plan and send the mutual action plan doc post-kickoff.

Best,
Marissa
